title: Without such grace no one could be saved
source_text: VII. Et certe, nisi Deus talem hominibus gratiam largiretur per quam possent verum & sincerum divinis mandatis obsequium praebere, nullus eorum salvus esse posset, & legitime confidere Deum erga ipsum usurum beneficentia & misericordia illa, quam nobis in Christo offert & exhibet. Nec enim Deus cum aliis misericorditer & benigne acturum sese pollicetur, quam cum iis qui foedus ejus servant, & mandata illius faciunt. Ut videre est, Psal. 103. Misericordia autem Domini ab aeterno & usque in aeternum super timentes eum: & justitia ejus in filios filiorum. His qui servant testamentum ejus, & memores sunt mandatorum ipsius ad faciendum ea. Quibus congruit illud quod legitur apud Ezechielem, cap. 18. Si autem impius egerit poenitentiam ab omnibus peccatis suis quae operatus est, & custodierit omnia praecepta mea, & fecerit judicium & justitiam: vita vivet & non morietur. Omnium iniquitatum ejus, quas operatus est non recordabor: in justitia sua quam operatus est vivet.
pass_a_gloss: VII. And certainly, unless God bestowed on men such grace through which they could render a true & sincere obedience to the divine commandments, none of them could be saved, & rightly trust that God will use toward him that beneficence & mercy, which he offers & shows us in Christ. For God does not promise that he will deal mercifully & kindly with any others, than with those who keep his covenant, & do his commandments. As may be seen, Psal. 103. But the mercy of the Lord is from eternity & to eternity upon those who fear him: & his righteousness unto children's children. To those who keep his covenant, & are mindful of his commandments to do them. With which agrees what is read in Ezekiel, chap. 18. But if the wicked man shall do penance for all his sins which he has committed, & shall keep all my precepts, & shall do judgment & righteousness: living he shall live & shall not die. Of all his iniquities, which he has committed I will not remember: in his righteousness which he has wrought he shall live.
pass_b_english: Thesis VII. Certainly, if God did not give people a grace by which they could offer his commandments true and sincere obedience, none of them could be saved, or have good grounds for trusting that God will show him the kindness and mercy he offers and grants us in Christ. God promises to deal mercifully and kindly only with those who keep his covenant and carry out his commandments.

So Psalm 103: 'The Lord's mercy is from everlasting to everlasting on those who fear him, and his righteousness reaches their children's children, those who keep his covenant and remember his commandments so as to do them.' Ezekiel 18 agrees: 'If the wicked man repents of all the sins he has committed, keeps all my precepts and does what is just and right, he will surely live; he will not die. I will not remember any of the wrongs he has done; he will live by the righteousness he has practised.'

lemmas.gloss: a true and sincere obedience to the divine commandments
living he shall live and shall not die

choices.why: Scripture's phrase for the obedience of believers, kept distinct from perfect fulfilment of the law.
